lines.text: Price data shows car insurance up 14.2% in 2022, then 20.3% in 2023.

lines.text: Then 11.3% in 2024 and 2.8% in 2025. Compounded, that's about 57%.
lines.say: Then eleven point three in twenty twenty-four and two point eight in twenty twenty-five. Compounded, that's about fifty-seven percent.

lines.text: Insurers were losing money on policies. In 2022, they spent about $112 on claims and costs for every $100 of premium.

lines.text: Repairs got pricier, cars got packed with sensors, and claims got bigger.

post.title: Car insurance jumped 57% in four years. Why?
post.ig:
Car insurance jumped 57% in four years. Why?
BLS price data: +14.2% in 2022, +20.3% in 2023, +11.3% in 2024, +2.8% in 2025 (December to December).
Why: insurers spent about $112 on claims and costs per $100 of premium in 2022 as repairs and claims got pricier, then raised rates. By 2025 it was about $92.
Prices eased 5.1% in the year to August 2026, a small dip after a big climb.
Sources: BLS Consumer Price Index; Triple-I personal auto results.
